subject: Performance & concurrency: post-call summary and next steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-27T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Performance & concurrency: post-call summary and next steps

Hi Chris / Ana —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick written recap so we have alignment and clear next steps on the performance/SLO side before we put together formal quota options.

What I captured from today:
- High-level goal: embed low-latency scoring into user experience (personalization flow).
- Target latency: p95 ~150–200ms for text-generation endpoints (non-streaming); streaming sessions need end-to-end latency under 250ms for first-byte.
- Concurrency: ~200 parallel short requests (peak), plus ~120 concurrent active streaming sessions during business hours.
- Burst profile: 15-minute window every hour with spikes to ~300 parallel short requests for 45–90s.
- Typical request size: 80–160 tokens in, ~60–200 tokens out; average token length ~120.

Immediate asks for us to size a recommended quota profile:
1) Confirm: is the 300-sustained spike an absolute peak or a recurring pattern you expect in production?
2) Send us a one-week sample traffic CSV (timestamp, req_type, in_tokens, out_tokens, stream_flag).
3) Any mandatory compliance constraints that would push you to Private deployment? (data residency / VPC)

Attached: redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf — high-level hosted vs dedicated rate options.

Proposed next steps:
- If you can share the traffic sample and confirm the burst characteristics, we’ll produce 2 profile options:
  A) Hosted API profile with conservative quotas + automated fallback (recommended for speed of launch)
  B) Dedicated-reserved profile (for predictable throughput & tighter SLO guarantees)
- Schedule 30m SLO alignment call (ops + infra) — suggest Tue or Wed next week.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Performance & concurrency: post-call summary and next steps

Thanks Kim — quick answers and a traffic summary attached inline. Ana looped on procurement.

Short answers:
- The 300 spike is recurring during batch-fanout (roughly every 40–90 minutes) and is a hard requirement; we need the service to sustain it without failed requests.
- We will send a one-week CSV by end of day (exporting now).
- Data residency: US only for now; not air-gapped — hosted is acceptable if we can get rate guarantees.

Traffic pattern (high level):
- Baseline: 60–80 qps sustained (non-peak)
- Peak: bursts to 300 qps for ~60s, recurring ~6–10x per day
- Streaming: ~120 concurrent sessions at peak; each session streams short deltas (~20–40 tokens every 2–4s) for an average live window of 2.5 minutes
- Token averages: 110 input / 140 output

Constraints / asks:
- p95 target: 200ms for short requests; first-byte for streaming within 250ms is preferred
- We need a clear fallback behavior if quotas are hit (throttling vs queueing vs degrade to smaller model)
- Procurement needs projected monthly spend range for both hosted and dedicated options

We attached a sanitized sample CSV (velox_sample_week.csv). Let me know if you need anything else.

—Chris
Chris Nguyen
Sr. Platform Engineer, Velox Financial
chris@veloxfinance.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Performance & concurrency: post-call summary and next steps

Chris — thanks for the sample. I ran a quick capacity sketch based on the CSV you sent and the targets you provided. High level proposals below — these are conservative starting points we can iterate on after a short load test.

Option 1 — Hosted (fastest on-ramp)
- Connection pool / parallel requests: soft cap 250 parallel requests per account, with burst allowance to 350 for 60–90s windows (burst tokens are rate-limited by account).
- Streaming sessions: 150 concurrent streaming sessions cap; session multiplexing allowed but each active session counts toward the cap.
- Token throughput guardrail: 50k tokens/minute per-account normal; auto-throttle if sustained above 80k for >5 minutes.
- Fallback behavior: configured policy — 1) queue up to 2s, 2) if queue full return 429 with transparent Retry-After, 3) if critical, route to smaller model variant (opt-compact) for degraded responses.
- Observability: per-route latency p95 / qps / token-rate dashboards; we’ll expose a token-level bill impact estimate.

Option 2 — Dedicated (SLA + predictable throughput)
- Provision a reserved pool sized for your 300qps spikes: we recommend base capacity for 350 concurrents with headroom for 20% burst (to match your pattern).
- Streaming: dedicated streaming shard(s) with 200 session capacity; persistent KV prefix cache enabled to reduce per-request cost for repeat prefixes.
- Rate-card: flat monthly commit + overage tokens at discounted rates; we’ll provide detailed numbers once we agree target capacity window.

Attachments: velox-quota-proposal.xlsx (spreadsheet with per-model TPUs / token bands / estimated monthly cost).

Immediate ask from our side:
- Can you confirm which endpoints will be latency-sensitive vs best-effort (a short list is fine: e.g., personalization-score, content-munge)?
- Propose two 30-minute windows next week for a short load test (we run synthetic traffic to your traffic shape).

If you’re okay with Option 1 we can spin a hosted quota profile and a staged throttling policy for a pilot next week. If you need an SLA-backed commit we’ll draft a Dedicated sizing + cost worksheet.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

Thanks all — a few implementation notes and a proposed timeline: 

Implementation notes:
- Connection pooling: we recommend client-side keep-alive + 8 multiplexed HTTP/2 streams per connection to minimize socket churn. Server-side we’ll maintain a per-account connection pool gate tied to the parallel-request cap.
- Prefix KV caching: enable for personalization keys to cut token cost by ~30% for repeat prefixes (we’ll need key TTL requirements from you).
- Load test plan: Redwood will run two synthetic runs that mimic your burst pattern (baseline + peak). Each run ~15 minutes. We’ll measure p95, tail, and model token throughput.

Proposed timeline:
- Oct 4–5: run baseline synthetic run (no procurement constraints)
- Oct 6: peak-burst synthetic run (simulate recurring 300 qps spikes)
- Oct 7: review results with Velox engineers and present recommended quota adjustments

I scheduled a 30m SLO alignment call: Oct 5, 10:00 AM PT. HubSpot link: https://hubspot.com/deal/VEL-1392 — please accept the invite if that works.

Rohan Mehta
